# The standard packages, series 0.3

<!-- Generated by scripts/skill/build.py from libraries/ and `rnl catalog`. Edit those, not this file. -->

What a file of RNL 0.3 can name without writing it: the definitions its statements fill (`@AS $NAME`), the symbols its instances are drawn with, and the sets it edits. The package `rnl-std` is used at the root of every file implicitly; the others are used by naming them in the header record. A name that is not in the packages in use is an error, and `rnl check` suggests the closest one. This reference is written from the package files of the series 0.3 and from the catalog of the `rnl` command, and is in step with them.

Using a package other than `rnl-std`, in the header record (the standard 16.2, 16.3, 16.5):

```rnl
@RNL(type="header") {
  @VERSION("0.3");
  @USE-PACKAGE(name="rnl-std-full", version="0.3")
}
```

## Packages

| Package | References | What it is for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `analog-canvas-extensions` 0.1 | – | The look variants of Analog Canvas and its chopper: Analog Canvas's own package, not part of the standard series. |
| `rnl-std` 0.3 (implicit) | `rnl-std-core`, `rnl-std-fill`, `rnl-std-structures` | The standard package, used at the root of every netlist by default. It only references other packages and has no content of its own. |
| `rnl-std-basic` 0.3 | – | The symbols of passive parts, sources, switches, transmission lines, virtual elements and marks; the definitions of the virtual and drawing-only parts, the ground and supply stubs, and the rules that draw them. |
| `rnl-std-core` 0.3 | `rnl-std-style`, `rnl-std-basic`, `rnl-std-semiconductors`, `rnl-std-spice`, `rnl-std-spectre` | The smallest collection: styles, symbols and the rules that give them, enough to draw the netlist and nothing more — no grounds, supplies or port tags filled in. |
| `rnl-std-fill` 0.3 | `rnl-std-basic` | The automatic fill: a ground or supply for every unwired pin on such a net; a port tag for every port net but the ground and supply nets, which have their grounds and supplies already; and the grounds of a ground net other than 0, such as vss, drawn with the name of the net under them. And the sets a file edits. |
| `rnl-std-full` 0.3 | `rnl-std`, `rnl-std-functional`, `rnl-std-rf`, `rnl-std-logic`, `rnl-std-signal-flow` | rnl-std with the four domain packages: functional, rf, logic and signal-flow. |
| `rnl-std-functional` 0.3 | – | Function blocks: op-amps, comparators, amplifiers, transconductors, ADC, DAC. |
| `rnl-std-logic` 0.3 | – | Logic gates, buffer, inverter, D flip-flops, and the drawing-only delay cell. |
| `rnl-std-no-labels` 0.3 | – | Turns off the default labels of the standard symbols, for files that write all their labels themselves. |
| `rnl-std-rf` 0.3 | – | RF parts: the centre-tapped inductor and the T-coil. |
| `rnl-std-semiconductors` 0.3 | – | The symbols of diodes, MOS transistors, BJTs and JFETs. |
| `rnl-std-signal-flow` 0.3 | – | Signal-flow blocks: adder and multiplier, and the drawing-only integrator, discrete-time integrator, quantizer and unit delay. |
| `rnl-std-spectre` 0.3 | `rnl-std-basic`, `rnl-std-semiconductors` | The symbol rules of Spectre netlists: primitives by master, instances of model cards by model type. |
| `rnl-std-spice` 0.3 | `rnl-std-basic`, `rnl-std-semiconductors` | The symbol rules of SPICE netlists: by element letter first, then by model type. |
| `rnl-std-structures` 0.3 | – | Structures: differential pair, current mirror, branch, chain, cascade, mirrored, flow and more. Some carry a default drawing, all of priority low: what the author writes comes first, and PRIORITY on a usage turns it off. |
| `rnl-std-style` 0.3 | – | The styles $base, $bus, $signal, $note and $grey, and the rules that give every kind of object its default style. |
| `rnl-zh` 0.3 | – | The Chinese alias package: Chinese spellings of the standard words and of the standard package's names, loaded with @USE-ALIASES in the header record. |

## Definitions

A definition is used as `#A(role) #B(role) @AS $DEFINITION` (the standard 9.5). A role in braces, such as `{tail}`, is a set: it takes any number of objects, none included. A role has a kind, which says what may fill it; parameters have defaults.

### rnl-std-basic

| Definition | Roles | Parameters (defaults) | Symbol | Comment before it in the file |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$GROUND` | `p` (net/terminal) | – | `$GROUND_SYMBOL` | virtual elements (12.5, 12.6, 13.2, 15.2). Their role is p (net is a standard subobject name, 9.4); ${p} shows the net, or the net of the terminal when drawn on a pin (13.6, PR1). |
| `$SUPPLY` | `p` (net/terminal) | – | `$SUPPLY_SYMBOL` |  |
| `$IO_PORT` | `p` (net/terminal) | – | `$IO_PORT_SYMBOL` |  |
| `$NO_CONNECT` | `t` (terminal) | – | `$NO_CONNECT_SYMBOL` |  |
| `$JUNCTION` | `p` (point/terminal) | – | `$JUNCTION_SYMBOL` |  |
| `$CURRENT_ARROW` | `p` (terminal/point) | – | `$CURRENT_ARROW_SYMBOL` |  |
| `$ARROW` | `p` (point) | – | `$ARROW_SYMBOL` | an arrow head on a point, in a symbol or in the scene (9.2.7) |
| `$SPDT_SWITCH` | `p` (point) | – | `$SPDT_SWITCH_SYMBOL` | a part that is only drawn and has no netlist line: a usage on a point (9.2.7, 13.4). A wire of a real net that ends on one of its pins ends at that point's coordinates. |
| `$FIGURE` | `p` (point) | – | – | any symbol drawn as a figure on a point, with no netlist line: each usage writes its own SET-SYMBOL; there is no default. Its pins have no terminals, as $SPDT_SWITCH's |
| `$GROUND_STUB` | `t` (terminal) | `gap` = `2.0` | – | ground and supply with their own wire, at least gap below or above a pin, pointing away from it; rnl-std-fill attaches them. Only the least distance is given, so that a solver may draw a stub longer, as when it lines up the grounds of … |
| `$SUPPLY_STUB` | `t` (terminal) | `gap` = `2.0` | – |  |

## Symbols

A symbol is chosen by the rules of the next section, or by `@SET-SYMBOL $NAME` on an object or a set. Pins are listed by terminal number with the direction a wire leaves in. The standard symbols are drawn in grid steps, y up.

## Which symbol an instance gets

The rules of `rnl-std-spice` and `rnl-std-spectre` give an instance its symbol; the narrow rules (by model type) come later than the broad ones and win. A file of SPICE uses the first, a file of Spectre the second (16.3).

## Chinese aliases

`rnl-zh` 0.3 gives Chinese spellings of the keywords, of the names above and of the parameters and roles of their definitions: 283 aliases, listed in `libraries/standard/0.3/rnl-zh.rnl` of the repository. A file loads it with `@USE-ALIASES(name="rnl-zh", version="0.3")` in the header record. Each alias reads as the standard word it stands for (16.5), so a file may mix both spellings, and the standard spellings keep working.
